newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RAM defends its record managing RPT.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RAM defends its record managing RPT.

text.p: Rural and Agricultural Management (RAM) defended its record managing Rural Property Trust on Monday and said it would propose the corporatisation of the group.

Earlier on Monday RPT's largest unit-holder, Bankers Trust International Plc (BTI), said it had requisitioned an extraordinary meeting of all unitholders to remove RAM as RPT's manager because of what it said was a poor profitability record.
"We are confident that year-end profitability will be substantially higher," a RAM spokesman told Reuters.

The spokesman said the RAM board had decided at a meeting last Thursday to propose the corporatisation of the trust, which would allow the creation of a board of unit-holders' representatives who would then directly appoint and control management.
"We would hope that the existing management and staff would be reappointed," he said.
He said RAM had presided over a rise in the unit price of RPT to 52 cents from 17 cents and had cut bank debt to zero.
RAM had changed RPT's investment stance in its rural properties to an active stance from a passive one and was currently turning around profitability at many of the properties.
"We are achieving strong increases in profitability from projects we are reviving," the spokesman said.
BT said earlier the trust has consistently underperformed, has traded significantly below its net tangible asset backing and has demonstrated a poor track record of profitability.

"We consider that management has failed to implement promised changes to its asset portfolio and corporate structure and we are very dissatisfied with the lack of progress on both counts," BT International managing director Lawrence Hudson said in a statement.

BT pointed to an aggregate net operating loss since June 30, 1991, RPT's unit price consistently trading at a discount of more than 20 percent to net tangible asset backing per unit and no dividend payments since listing in 1994.
The RAM spokesman said RPT could not pay dividends because it still had substantial tax losses to use up.
RPT closed down two cents at 42 cents on Friday and was untraded on Monday. RPT's net asset backing at December 31 was 55.11 cents.
RPT reported a A$2.35 million profit for the six months to December 31 1996 last month, compared with a A$2.81 million loss in the same half a year earlier.
